newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovaks cooling to NATO membership - poll.
newsitem.headline: Slovaks cooling to NATO membership - poll.

text.p: Slovaks are cooling towards NATO membership with slightly more than a third in favour, according to the latest opinion poll by the Slovak Statistics Bureau (SUSR).
Asked in the first weekend of December how they would vote, only 35.1 percent said they supported membership, 25.5 percent said they were against and 28.1 percent were undecided.
In a SUSR poll last June, 44 percent of respondents supported NATO membership compared with 30 percent against.

Slovakia is keen to be among the first new members of NATO and the European Union but some analysts say its chances are waning because of Western concern over the slow pace of the government's democratic reforms.
NATO is to hold a summit in Madrid in July to nominate the first candidates for membership and the Czech Republic, Poland and Hungary are seen as the leading contenders.
In the latest Slovak poll, 88.7 percent of the 1,269 people asked said they would take part in a referendum.
By law, more than 50 percent of eligible voters must take part for it to be valid, and a majority of participants are needed to carry the decision.
"The final number of those who would agree with Slovakia's NATO membership remains strongly influenced by the number of undecided," SUSR said.
